newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Cable perky, keeping above $1.6550 key.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Cable perky, keeping above $1.6550 key.

text.p: Sterling is looking up against the dollar after breaking above key resistance of $1.6550 overnight, and chartists said cable should head higher if it can manage to stay above that level.

"Overall, the tone for sterling against the dollar is looking a lot better since it broke above the old highs at $1.6550, which we hit at the beginning of April," said Marc Ostwald, technical analyst at London Bond Broking.
"The key for cable is whether we will be able to close above that level today, which would negate a potential double-top scenario," Ostwald said.
Sterling was trading at $1.6580/90 at 0755 GMT against $1.6440/50 in late Europe on Tuesday.

Analysts saw the next goal for sterling at around $1.6650, which they said was an area of major congestion. A break there should trigger a rise to further congestion around $1.6730, dating back to December, they said.
On the downside, last week's high just below $1.6500 should provide support, with a break below setting up $1.6430, where cable was capped on Friday and Monday, chartists said.
Meanwhile, sterling/mark looked set to test above 2.8000, although no surges were expected for now.
Sterling/mark was at 2.8003/13 at 0810 GMT against late Tuesday's 2.7853/63.

"The implications are quite bullish implying a break of (the previous cycle high of) 2.8345 marks, opening upside potential to 2.8500/20, represented by the upper boundary of the ascending trend channel intervening on weekly charts," said Chase Investment Bank's technical analysis team.

Analysts said sterling/mark would face initial resistance at a congestion level around 2.8045-60. On the downside 2.7780, sterling's old floor in the European exchange rate mechanism, would provide firm support, they said.
